title: Structured-process agent desktop workspace
prompt: Add a native FluentQt desktop client to an existing structured-process agent runtime. Preserve the existing runtime entry point. The client must support one real run, streamed assistant output, tool and permission events, cancellation, retry, an empty state, and a narrow layout.
required_product_evidence: The target repository's process protocol and lifecycle
The durable result or primary run object
Subject materials, artifacts, instruments, verbs, and workflow tempo
Explicit user and project taste signals plus one non-UI subject reference
At least one aligned and one contrastive product reference
One justified aesthetic risk with a quiet zone, usability guard, and fallback
A genericity critique with at least one concrete subject-specific revision
One coherent icon family with provenance, reuse-or-generation decision, application-tile and in-product-mark strategies, small-size evidence, state, and accessibility rules
One approved identity anchor expanded into restrained Light and Dark semantic roles
One product-copy policy with direct voice, shared state vocabulary, compression rules, and localization behavior
A full-profile architecture manifest with app, domain, application, infrastructure, and UI layers
A composition-only shell under the configured line and member budgets
Layer-mirrored controller, adapter, model, and UI tests
One shared representative-content fixture and three high-fidelity full-window comps
A recorded human concept decision before production UI code
An implementation design system extracted from the accepted concept
The final built application in Light, Dark, narrow, and minimum states
design_intelligence_checks: The primary surface communicates the product object and time model without relying on a logo or accent color.
The selected concept could not be reused unchanged for an unrelated desktop product.
The controlled aesthetic risk is visible but does not weaken text, focus, keyboard, IME, localization, or native behavior.
The implementation preserves the accepted concept's container model, hierarchy, typography roles, state grammar, and signature move.
Material deviations from the accepted full-window and detail comps are recorded and justified.
Product-owned copy names objects, states, and actions without assistant narration or repeated explanation.
Each visible operation has one owning region and primary entry; wide and narrow fallbacks are mutually exclusive.
The packaged application tile, transparent in-product mark, and semantic palette visibly belong to one restrained identity system.
At 1x in a representative wide active state, primary content keeps a readable measure and scale; large quiet regions have an explicit role rather than separating the transcript from its composer.
The promised signature move is visibly legible in final pixels without a logo, zoom, annotation, or design-brief explanation.
engineering_checks: The project-structure validator passes in strict mode.
The shell owns window composition and platform events, not protocol parsing, process launch, settings validation, or demo generation.
Domain and application layers do not import Qt Widgets or FluentQt.
The structured-process adapter owns process and protocol lifetime behind an application-facing boundary.
Growing events use a bounded model and delegate rather than one child widget per event.
Both cross-agent runs resolve the same pinned FluentQt dependency, and an actual Inspector report is produced; an unavailable compatibility placeholder fails the check.
anti_shortcuts: Do not expose raw protocol method names or identifiers as the main transcript copy.
Do not render every event kind as the same rounded card with a different label.
Do not present a concept that could fit an unrelated app by changing only its logo and copy.
Do not replace the controlled aesthetic risk with a generic safe shell during implementation.
Do not mix icon packs, emoji, arbitrary glyphs, or unlicensed screenshot-derived assets.
Do not replace a valid upstream mark with an unreviewed generated icon or reuse a transparent title glyph as the packaged application tile.
Do not turn one sampled logo color into every pane, border, action, and status role.
Do not leave two simultaneously visible controls wired to the same operation merely because they occupy different regions.
Do not fill sparse space with assistant narration, procedural headings, duplicated help, or generic marketing copy.
Do not call a wide active layout intentional when useful content is compressed into a shallow edge strip and the fixed composer is separated by an unowned dead field.
Do not count a signature described in the brief when it is not recognizable at 1x in the final application.
Do not keep a permanent navigation rail unless several stable destinations justify it.
Do not default-select the first recipe or treat a schematic SVG as a high-fidelity comp.
Do not let the implementation agent record human concept approval.
Do not let the implementation agent perform the final visual review.
Do not split a God window into partial source files while preserving the same unrelated ownership.
Do not add broad source-root exceptions or raise architecture budgets to make validation pass.
Do not treat build, functional tests, or manifest validation as aesthetic acceptance.
cross_agent_runs: Cursor with the same installed Skill package
